title: [YouPass Collect] - International tourism spending by country comparison
prompt: The chart below shows the amount of money in billions of dollars spent on international tourism by people from seven different countries in 2011 and 2012. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart compares the expenditure on international tourism by travellers from seven countries in 2011 and 2012.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, spending increased in most of the given countries during this period, with the exception of Germany and France. In addition, China witnessed by far the most substantial growth, surpassing all other nations to become the leading spender by 2012.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the top three spenders, in 2011, Germany allocated the highest budget for overseas travel at 82 billion dollars, exceeding the US and China, which spent approximately 78 billion and 73 billion respectively. Over the following year, China's expenditure surged dramatically by 32 billion to reach 105 billion dollars, making it the dominant spender and far outpacing the other two nations. Meanwhile, the US saw a modest rise of 2 billion, ending at 80 billion, whereas Germany experienced a slight decline to the same figure, resulting in both countries having identical spending levels.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining nations, the UK spent 46 billion dollars in 2011, which was 6 billion higher than France at 40 billion. Russia and Canada expended considerably less, at around 29 billion and 19 billion respectively. By 2012, both the UK and Russia had increased their tourism budgets, reaching exactly 50 billion and 40 billion dollars in that order. Conversely, France's spending dropped slightly to 38 billion, whilst Canada's expenditure remained stable at 19 billion dollars.
